analysis: Cross-source read: the first 30 minutes belong to the AI-demand bid with the rate ceiling holding. The durable goods print (unchanged vs -0.3% expected) is a non-event for the tape: neither hot enough to re-press the long end nor soft enough to crack the 10Y below the 5.15-5.21% zone it tested Thursday, so the October-hike pricing (~75% in futures, 95% for at least one more hike by year-end per CME FedWatch) stands. The real action is structural: AKAM +14% at the open on the $11.6B Anthropic commitment is the confirmed revenue datapoint behind this week's AI tape, META is cooling (-2.5%) after its +4.5% Thursday sprint toward all-time highs, and the Intel 14A report (evaluating, not committing) is a diversification-of-supply story more than an Intel turn story. The 15.61% NVDA+AAPL index weight is why the AI bid moves the whole benchmark and why META's wobble mattered more than the Dow's composition today. What changed vs the 6 AM brief: the durable goods print now has a confirmed number (in-line, slightly firm); Schmid has spoken (inflation-first, no October commitment); oil and the 10Y both ticked down into the open; AKAM held roughly two-thirds of its premarket spike; COST bounced +1% on the beat; Meta faded. Signal vs noise: the open moves, the durable goods print, AKAM deal terms, META's move, Costco's reported Q4 figures, and the Fed-official quotes are confirmed across outlets; the Intel 14A evaluation list and the Hormuz deal path are single-source/talks-in-progress, treat as fragile.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Indexes opened higher with relief on yields and oil: S&P 500 +0.2%, Nasdaq Composite +0.2%, Dow +0.2% (+167 pts) per Barron's; Investopedia ticked the open at Nasdaq +0.2%, S&P +0.1%, Dow +0.1%. Weekly: S&P +0.7% and Nasdaq +1.6% are on track for a second straight weekly gain, while the Dow is -0.6% and on pace for its fourth straight weekly loss.
headlines.why_it_matters: Green open off a modest yield/oil pullback, but the bid stays narrow: AI infra plus lower yields, not broad participation, and the Dow is diverging from the index on its weekly line.

headlines.headline: August durable goods orders were essentially unchanged: -$0.1B to $338.6B (roughly 0.0%) vs WSJ consensus of -0.3%, after a +0.9% July. Transportation equipment fell 0.6% (down three of the last four months); excluding defense, new orders rose 0.1%.
headlines.why_it_matters: A neutral-for-yields print: slightly firmer than feared but too flat to move the hike odds either way, so the data-dependent standoff with the Fed continues into the next release.

headlines.headline: The 10Y sat at 5.19% into the open, down about 2 bps from Thursday's close, after Thursday's run to the highest level since 2007 (19-year high, ~18 bps higher on the week). Oil fell with it: WTI -2.1% to $92.60, Brent -1.7% to $104.80, on the Reuters report of US-Iran talks toward reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Gold +0.5% to $4,320; BTC around $84,100; DXY ~100.9.
headlines.why_it_matters: The two variables that capped the week, yields and oil, are both easing into Friday's close, which is why equities can firm even with the hiking drumbeat intact; a stalled Hormuz negotiation would reverse both quickly.

headlines.headline: Fed officials sounded nowhere near done: CME FedWatch priced a 95% chance of at least one more hike across the year's final two meetings; KC Fed's Schmid said inflation is his primary concern with growth resilient; Philly's Paulson backed 'modest further tightening'; Williams called another 2026 hike 'reasonable'; Hammack warned fuel-driven inflation risks an 'inflationary mindset' and speaks again at 2 PM ET today.
headlines.why_it_matters: Five officials this week and zero stop signals, so the market keeps pricing a probability, not a plan; that keeps the ceiling on growth multiples into every data point regardless of the morning's green tape.

headlines.headline: Meta fell 2.5% at the open after Thursday's 4.5% surge toward an all-time high on the Connect AI products (Muse assistant, Charm device), and the Magnificent Seven ETF (MAGS) slipped 0.3%. Reuters had it flat premarket, on track for a fifth straight weekly gain and less than 1% from a $2T market cap.
headlines.why_it_matters: Classic gravity on a parabolic consumer-AI run; the $2T milestone is still the tape's magnet, and with Meta near index-driver weight, its wobble mattered more than most single-name moves.

headlines.headline: Akamai soared 14% at the bell after Anthropic committed to at least $11.6B over seven years for cloud infrastructure and software, with a potential $9B expansion (up to ~$20B total). Anthropic also got a warrant for up to 7.7M shares (~5%) at $111.33/share, valued ~$857.2M. JPMorgan raised its target to $167 (from $158), neutral; Oppenheimer kept outperform/$180; AKAM was up ~27% YTD heading into Friday.
headlines.why_it_matters: A confirmed hard-revenue AI-infra deal, not a narrative, which is why it holds a double-digit bid and anchors the AI-demand side of this week's capex debate; the warrant gives Anthropic aligned equity upside.

headlines.headline: Piper Sandler research (via TechSpot) says Amazon, Apple, AMD, Google, Tesla, Microsoft, Nvidia, and Qualcomm are all evaluating Intel's 14A chipmaking process; the firm says Intel needs an anchor customer in late 2026 or early 2027 before a planned 2028 ramp, noting TSMC capacity is sold out through 2028. No customer has announced a commitment.
headlines.why_it_matters: Single-source relay of an analyst note, unconfirmed beyond it, treat as fragile; evaluating is not committing, but the list shows the majors want non-Taiwan supply options, which is a demand-diversification angle for the whole complex.

headlines.headline: Nvidia (8.21%) and Apple (7.40%) now command a combined 15.61% of the S&P 500, the heaviest two-stock concentration on record, with the top 10 holdings at 38.69% (ETF holdings as of Sept 23, via parameter.io/coincentral). AAPL hit $345 this week on the iPhone 18 and first foldable iPhone Duo; NVDA closed Thursday at $224.58, up ~20-21% YTD.
headlines.why_it_matters: Structural, not tactical: the AI bid moves the whole benchmark because two names are one-sixth of it, which is why Meta's 2.5% open fade mattered more than the Dow's green line and why index breadth stays deceptively weak.

headlines.headline: Costco bounced 1% higher at the open after its Q4 beat (revenue $95.72B vs $94.86B est, EPS $6.75 vs $6.54 est), following a flat after-hours reaction on the detail: $0.15/share of the EPS came from one-off IEEPA tariff refunds and membership-fee income growth slowed to 7.3%, the third straight quarterly deceleration.
headlines.why_it_matters: The morning bid forgave the quality discount on the beat (refund-flattered EPS, slowing membership metric), so the open says the retail tape is willing to pay for a defensive compounder while yields stay high.

market_snapshot.breadth_notes: At the open: S&P 500 +0.2%, Nasdaq +0.2%, Dow +0.2% (+167 pts, Barron's); Investopedia ticked Nasdaq +0.2%, S&P +0.1%, Dow +0.1%. Weekly: S&P +0.7%, Nasdaq +1.6% on track for 2nd straight weekly gains; Dow -0.6% on pace for 4th straight weekly loss. S&P 500 A/D ratio, volume vs 20-day average, and sector breadth were not shown in sourced pages.
market_snapshot.notes: First 30 minutes of the session: the AI bid (AKAM +14%, chips firm) plus easing yields and oil carried the open against a ~75% October-hike print. The durable goods print landed in-line/slightly firm and moved nothing. 10Y 5.19%, -2 bps from Thursday's close (vs 5.176% in the prior brief). META faded -2.5% after Thursday's +4.5%; COST +1% on the beat.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC news this morning; carried context stands: the Sept 9/10 $600M 6.75% senior notes pricing (due 2035, net ~$592M to repay credit borrowings) and the NYSE-to-TXSE listing transfer (NYSE trading ends Oct 2, TXSE begins Oct 5, ticker unchanged). Q2 recap: revenue $342.1M, adjusted EBITDA $193.2M, DCF coverage 1.65x, $0.525 distribution, full-year guidance confirmed (EBITDA $770-800M, DCF $480-510M). Units open into a softer oil tape (Brent -1.7% to ~$104.8), a modest sector tailwind for the Friday session.

watch_next: 10:00 AM ET: Michigan consumer sentiment final (prelim 47.8, consensus 47.8) — watch for a confirmed number and any yield reaction.
2:00 PM ET: Cleveland Fed's Hammack speaks; watch for any October-commitment language against the ~75% priced odds.
The 10Y vs the 5.15-5.21% zone: does the -2 bps open relief hold into the close or fade like Thursday's?
Does the AKAM bid hold into the close and does META recover toward the $2T line; the MAGS -0.3% shows megacap breadth is thin.
Any confirmation or denial of the US-Iran Hormuz talks progress — the single biggest swing factor for oil and inflation expectations next week.
